implementation_notes: WCF's System.ServiceModel.Channels.Message is the pattern as a framework type: Headers exposes a MessageHeaders collection and the static CreateMessage overloads attach a body (object, byte array, BodyWriter or fault) together with a MessageVersion - literally a header section plus a body package. For HTTP-shaped boundaries the BCL pair System.Net.Http.HttpRequestMessage/HttpResponseMessage plays the same role, with Headers for metadata and Content (HttpContent) for the body; the documentation also states that an instance must not be modified or reused after being sent, which is the immutable-package rule in .NET terms. Hand-writing a Message-like class is justified only when the framework does not model your wire shape (a fixed binary protocol, or a broker whose client library already defines its own message type).
pitfalls: A Message (and an HttpRequestMessage) must not be reused or modified after it has been sent; rebuilding per attempt is required, and reusing the instance across retries throws or corrupts state.
Both Message and the Http* types are IDisposable and buffer bodies: failing to dispose the original after copying/buffering leaks the underlying stream or content.
MessageHeaders.Add appends without replacing, so adding the same header name twice silently produces duplicates that downstream routing may resolve differently than intended.
